title: platform-safety-cage-and-experimentation-guidelines-2026
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary:
This document defines the "Platform Safety Cage": a standardized set of controls, observability requirements, and runbook steps for running any experiment that could impact platform availability, SLOs, or tenant economics. It covers synthetic workload simulation, controlled rollouts (canaries/A-B), chaos/latency injection, and resource policy experiments.

Scope:
- Applies to platform teams and services under eng-platform ownership (scheduler, router, autoscaler, prefix cache, billing pipeline).
- Does NOT cover purely client-side UX experiments (those should follow product AB testing guidelines).
- Includes both sandbox lab experiments and production canaries where traffic-steering is used.

Goals:
- Minimize blast radius and customer impact during experiments.
- Ensure experiments are observable, reversible, and documented.
- Provide prescriptive gates (SLO/alert thresholds) and an escalation matrix.

Owner and Roles:
- Safety Cage Owner: Maya Patel (eng-platform).
- Experiment Lead: person proposing/running the experiment (rotates per experiment).
- Observability Lead: SRE on shift who owns dashboards and alerts for the experiment.
- Emergency Responder: oncall eng-sre for the region.
- Reviewers: security/finance when experiment affects data residency or billing.

Safety Cage Concept (high level):
The Safety Cage is implemented as four concentric controls:
1) Prep (simulation + review) — Offline verification in sandbox, cost estimate, and risk assessment.
2) Bake (guardrail creation) — Dashboards, canary buckets, rate limits, and preconfigured rollback targets.
3) Execute (controlled rollout) — Automated slow ramp, active monitoring, and automated halting policies.
4) Recover (rollback & postmortem) — Fast rollback procedure and incident write-up.

Prerequisites (must be satisfied before any production experiment):
- Experiment proposal accepted in the weekly platform experiments board (link internal).
- Experiment runbook checked into the experiments registry with owner, start time, and expected duration.
- Observability: a dashboard with at minimum the metrics below and alerts attached.
- Feature flag toggles and traffic-slicing config exist and are validated in staging.
- Budget guardrail set (cost estimate + spend cap) if experiment influences reserved capacity or GPUs.

Minimum Observability Requirements (dashboards and alerts):
- Dashboards must include: P50/P95/P99 latency by route, token emission rate, tokens-per-request, KV cache hit ratio, request error rate (4xx/5xx), GPU utilization per pool, billing tokens-per-tenant.
- Automated alerts (severity/threshold):
  - Sev P0: overall request error rate > 3% for 5m OR P99 latency > 2x baseline for 3m.
  - Sev P1: P95 latency degrades > 1.5x baseline for 10m.
  - Cost Guard: spend delta vs projected > 25% over 1h.
  - Cache Storm: KV cache miss ratio increase > 30% relative to baseline for 15m.
- SLI gates (must be defined in the experiment runbook): the experiment must auto-halt if any SLI gate trips.

Experiment Classification (quick guide):
- Low-risk: non-production-only synthetic tests, staging-only configs. Approval: safety owner signoff.
- Medium-risk: production canary with <1% traffic impact, read-only workloads. Approval: Safety owner + Observability lead.
- High-risk: production experiments affecting traffic shaping, autoscaling, dedicated pools, or billing. Approval: Senior eng-platform manager + Security and Finance reviews.

Step-by-step: Running a controlled experiment (canonical workflow)
1) Proposal and sandbox simulation
   - Create a short experiment proposal in the experiments board with motivation, hypothesis, and KPIs.
   - Run synthetic workload in sandbox using the experiment generator tool (see appendix). Capture baseline metrics.
2) Preflight checklist (must pass)
   - Observability dashboard created and pinned
   - Feature flags and canary slices configured (namespace + tenant IDs)
   - Rollback artifacts ready (flag off, routing rule revert script, capacity autoscale back-to-normal script)
   - Pager duty aware and oncall informed
3) Canary execution
   - Start canary at 0.1% traffic for 10 minutes.
   - If no SLI gate trips, increase to 1% for 20 minutes.
   - Then increase to 5% for 30 minutes.
   - Use automated ramp tooling (platform canary-orchestrator) and enable auto-halt on SLI gate.
4) Gradual ramp and monitoring
   - Monitor for anomalous patterns in latency and token cost per tenant.
   - Hold at each step for at least 2x the 95th percentile tail latency measurement window.
5) Full rollout or rollback
   - If gates clear, proceed to production rollout per rollout policy. If a gate trips, auto-halt triggers and a human review is required within 10 minutes.

Traffic and Resource Controls (examples):
- Rate limit policy: per-tenant token rate caps and tenant-level burst tokens.
- CPU/GPU isolation: use cgroup limits and node taints for experimental pods.
- Priority classes: experiment pods must use lower priority class to allow preemption.
- Billing safety: spoken-of pockets: cost caps enforced per experiment with automatic pod eviction when budget breached.

Table: Example guardrail configuration (YAML-like fields shown for clarity)
| field | description | example |
|---|---:|---|
| canary_slice | percentage of total traffic assigned | 1% |
| auto_halt_sli | SLI name to auto-halt on | p99_latency_global |
| budget_cap_usd | experiment spend cap for duration | 500 |
| priority_class | K8s priority class for experiment pods | low-experiment |

Appendix: example configs and CLI commands
- Canary orchestration manifest (simplified):

apiVersion: platform.redwood/v1
kind: CanaryExperiment
metadata:
  name: kv-cache-miss-test-2026-02
spec:
  trafficSlices:
    - name: canary-a
      percent: 1
      tenantSelector: "labels.experiment==kvtest"
  autoHaltSLI: p99_latency_global
  budgetCapUsd: 500
  priorityClass: low-experiment

- Quick rollback commands (examples):
  - Disable feature flag:
    $ rdx-ff toggle --flag kv-prefetch-experiment --off --env prod --reason "rollback: slu"
  - Revert routing rule (CLI):
    $ rdx-router revert --rule-id rule-673 --to-tag stable --region us-west-2
  - Scale down experiment pool (k8s):
    $ kubectl scale deployment experiment-pool --replicas=0 -n platform-experiments

Safety automation: auto-halt mechanics
- Auto-halt is implemented in the canary-orchestrator service. Rules are simple boolean triggers: when any linked SLI breaches its configured threshold for the configured duration, canary-orchestrator flips the canary flag to OFF and posts the event to the experiments audit stream.
- Engineering must ensure the experiment manifest includes exact SLI names and alert policy IDs.

Rollback and postmortem expectations
- When an auto-halt or manual rollback occurs, the experiment lead must:
  1) Launch an incident in the platform incidents tracker (tag: experiment-rollbacks).
  2) Notify oncall SRE and product engineering.
  3) Capture heap/profile traces and relevant traces (X-Ray/OTEL) for the 10 minutes prior to the trip.
  4) Produce a short postmortem within 3 business days with root cause and action items.

Experiment Registry and Documentation
- All experiments must be logged to the experiments registry (Confluence page + experiments DB) including: hypothesis, KPIs, start/end time, owner, rollback steps, and link to dashboards.
- For recurring experiments (e.g., monthly scalability tests), create a recurring entry and tag previous runs in related_pages.

Retrospective cadence and metrics
- Monthly experiment review: a 1-hour retrospective run by the Safety Cage Owner covering failures, near-misses, and successes. Metrics to surface: number of auto-halts, average time-to-rollback, cost delta per experiment, and customer impact incidents.

FAQ (short)
Q: Can I run chaos tests directly in production?
A: Only if they are classified as low-risk or medium-risk with appropriate approvals and budget guardrails. High-risk production chaos requires executive-level approval.

Q: Who can trigger an emergency rollback?
A: The experiment lead, Observability Lead, or oncall eng-sre can trigger rollback. If none respond within 10 minutes of an auto-halt, the Safety Cage Owner escalates to platform director.
